entities.name: Jean-Camille Formigé
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Jean-Camille Formigé was a French architect during the French Third Republic. He served as the chief architect of historic monuments of France, and also as the chief architect of buildings, promenades and gardens of the city of Paris. His son, Jules Formigé, was also a prominent architect.
